findings.issue: stream_options.include_usage is only inserted when the client sent no stream_options; a client stream_options without include_usage:true yields an upstream stream with no usage frame, so gateway cost/budget accounting falls back to token estimates (stream:false previously returned real usage).
findings.fix: When stream_upstream is true, merge include_usage:true into an existing stream_options object, and restore the client's original value on the DD4 stream:false fallback.

findings.issue: The DD4 one-shot stream:false fallback is a `continue` inside `0..=max_retries`, so it never runs with max_retries_per_provider: 0 (or after an earlier retry used the budget); a provider rejecting stream_options then fails every buffered request.
findings.fix: Let the one-shot fallback run without consuming the retry budget (e.g. extend the loop bound once when it fires), or document that the opt-out is required in that configuration.

findings.issue: is_stream_param_rejection matches any 400 body containing 'stream' (after removing 'upstream'), so unrelated 400s that echo the word waste one stream:false retry.
findings.fix: Match parameter-shaped phrases (stream_options, quoted 'stream'/"stream", 'stream is not supported') instead of a bare substring.

findings.issue: relay_failure_class/relay_failure_attempt were inserted between is_transient_stream_truncation's doc comment and its fn (~4731-4752), so the truncation docs now attach to relay_failure_class and is_transient_stream_truncation is undocumented.
findings.fix: Move relay_failure_class and relay_failure_attempt above the is_transient_stream_truncation doc block.

findings.issue: The key guard tests read_upstream_body directly; no dispatch-level test streams a slow body through dispatch_attempts_under_permit, so mis-wired first-byte/idle/total deadlines or a bypassed reader would not fail any test.
findings.fix: Add a dispatch test against a small local streaming server that sends chunks spaced below the idle window for longer than ttfb_timeout_seconds and asserts success.
